riptideRemoval.title: Removal by the Numbers
riptideRemoval.author: Riptide Lab forum (discussing the Ars Arcanum 'History of Removal' analysis)

setSize.quote: The sets have the same number of unique cards (261), but 20 cards have shifted from common to uncommon.
setSize.note: The 81/100/60/20 split is tabulated from the same article by the mtgscribe fact sheet; 81+100+60+20 = 261 matches the article's stated total.

booster.quote: one of those cards is a land, nine are commons, three are uncommons, and one is a rare or mythic rare
booster.note: mythicOneInN=7 from the same article's 'six over seven, as every seventh booster could have a mythic rare'. This is the article's own simplified Play Booster model, not the full retail collation.

colors.W.common.creatures.quote: the default for Play Boosters is 73% (11 out of 15)

colors.W.common.creatureCurve.quote: White common creature slots: 1 at MV 1, 3 at MV 2, 3 at MV 3, 2 at MV 4, 1 at MV 5-6, 1 at MV 6-7 (total 11)
colors.W.common.creatureCurve.note: Curve buckets are tabulated by mtgscribe from the article's slot list; bucket counts sum to the article's stated 11 creatures.

colors.W.common.creatureShare.quote: The default for Draft Boosters was 63% (12 out of 19) while the default for Play Boosters is 73% (11 out of 15).
colors.W.common.creatureShare.note: Stated numerator/denominator are the article's own; 11/15 = 0.733 is consistent with the published slot tables (11 creatures + 4 spells = 15 white commons).

colors.W.common.avgPower.quote: In Draft Boosters, white's default average power was 2.95. In Play Boosters, that goes up to 3.28.

colors.W.common.keywords.quote: 3 Flying (different powers); 2 Vigilance; 1 Lifelink (low power); 0.25 First strike; 0.20 Double strike
colors.W.common.keywords.note: Fractional counts encode rotating slots shared across sets; enforce as set-level sums, never per card.

colors.W.common.spellSlots.quote: Combat removal 1; Exiling removal 1; Combat trick 1; Enchantment/Artifact removal 1 (total 4)

colors.U.common.creatures.quote: Blue creature percentages have gone up, but not as much as white, from 47% (9 out of 19) to 53% (8 out of 15).

colors.U.common.creatureCurve.quote: Blue common creature slots: 2 at MV 2, 3 at MV 3, 1 at MV 4, 1 at MV 5-6, 1 at MV 6-7 (total 8)
colors.U.common.creatureCurve.note: Blue has no one-drop creature slot in this skeleton.

colors.U.common.creatureShare.quote: from 47% (9 out of 19) to 53% (8 out of 15)
colors.U.common.creatureShare.note: 8/15 = 0.533, consistent with the published slot tables (8 creatures + 7 spells = 15 blue commons).

colors.U.common.avgPower.quote: The average power has gone up from 3.39 to 3.62.

colors.U.common.keywords.quote: 3 Flying (different powers); 1.5 Vigilance; 0.5 Ward N; 0.5 Defender; 0.5 Flash

colors.U.common.spellSlots.quote: Protective Instant; Counterspell; Cantrip; Draw (2-3 cards); Overwriting Aura removal; Top/Bottom spell; Modal spell (total 7)

colors.B.common.creatures.quote: Black's creature percentages have jumped from 52% (10 out of 19) to 62% (9 out of 14)

colors.B.common.creatureCurve.quote: Black common creature slots: 1 at MV 1-2, 2 at MV 2, 2 at MV 3, 1 at MV 4, 1 at MV 4-5, 1 at MV 5-6, 1 at MV 6-7 (total 9)

colors.B.common.creatureShare.quote: Black's creature percentages have jumped from 52% (10 out of 19) to 62% (9 out of 14)
colors.B.common.creatureShare.note: DISCREPANCY, verified 2026-08-09: the article's own fraction 9/14 evaluates to 0.643, not the stated 0.62, and the published slot tables give black 15 commons (9 creatures + 6 spells), i.e. 0.60. The slot tables are self-consistent (5 colors x 15 + 6 colorless = 81 commons, the article's stated total), so consumers should prefer the derived share over the stated one.

colors.B.common.avgPower.quote: its average power has jumped from 3.25 to 3.56.

colors.B.common.spellSlots.quote: Small conditional removal; Combat trick; Card draw (additional cost); Discard (you choose); Unconditional removal; Slightly overcosted removal (total 6)

colors.R.common.creatures.quote: Red has the second-largest increase in creature percentages at common, jumping from 53% (10 out of 19) to 64% (9 out of 14).

colors.R.common.creatureCurve.quote: Red common creature slots: 1 at MV 1-2, 2 at MV 2, 2 at MV 3, 1 at MV 3-4, 1 at MV 4-5, 1 at MV 5, 1 at MV 6 (total 9)

colors.R.common.creatureShare.quote: jumping from 53% (10 out of 19) to 64% (9 out of 14)
colors.R.common.creatureShare.note: DISCREPANCY, verified 2026-08-09: 9/14 = 0.643 matches the stated 0.64, but the published slot tables give red 15 commons (9 creatures + 6 spells), i.e. 0.60. Prefer the derived share.

colors.R.common.avgPower.quote: Its power has jumped from an average of 3.15 to 3.39.

colors.R.common.keywords.quote: 1.5 Trample; 1.5 Menace; 1.5 Haste; 1 Reach; 0.25 First strike; 0.20 Double strike

colors.R.common.spellSlots.quote: Direct damage (2); Combat trick; Card draw (discard/exile); Modal artifact destruction; Direct damage (~4); Direct damage (6 for 5 mana) (total 6)

colors.G.common.creatures.quote: Green has the largest creature percentage increase, going from 58% (11 out of 19) to 71% (10 out of 14).

colors.G.common.creatureCurve.quote: Green common creature slots: 1 at MV 1-2, 2 at MV 2, 2 at MV 3, 1 at MV 3-4, 1 at MV 4-5, 1 at MV 5, 1 at MV 6, 1 at MV 6-7 (total 10)

colors.G.common.creatureShare.quote: going from 58% (11 out of 19) to 71% (10 out of 14)
colors.G.common.creatureShare.note: DISCREPANCY, verified 2026-08-09: 10/14 = 0.714 matches the stated 0.71, but the published slot tables give green 15 commons (10 creatures + 5 spells), i.e. 0.667. Prefer the derived share.

colors.G.common.avgPower.quote: Its average power rose slightly from 3.59 to 3.7.

colors.G.common.keywords.quote: 1.5 Vigilance; 1.5 Trample; 1.5 Reach; 1 Deathtouch; 0.5 Ward N; 0.20 Haste

colors.G.common.spellSlots.quote: Fight; Bite; Combat trick (pump power); Mana acceleration; Dig (lands/creatures) (total 5)

colorless.common.quote: Colorless common creatures: variance buster (2 mana), three-mana creature, four-mana creature (total 3). Colorless common spells: removal (expensive), mana-producing artifact, land fixing (total 3).

multicolorUncommon.quote: One of the biggest changes from Draft Boosters to Play Boosters was the decision to increase from one multicolor card per two-color combination to two.
multicolorUncommon.note: 20 total uncommon multicolor slots, 2 per pair, conventionally split enabler + payoff.

archetypes.pairs.quote: If you're just starting out, I would focus on the ten two-color pairs.

archetypes.speedMix.quote: We divide into three speeds: fast, medium, and slow. You want at least three of each speed, with one getting a fourth.
archetypes.speedMix.note: flex=1 encodes 'one getting a fourth'; the fourth may land on any of the three speeds.

archetypes.noveltyMix.quote: you usually have about two archetypes that are doing something novel, four archetypes that are riffing off something they normally do but in a way that's a little different, and four archetypes that are doing something pretty familiar

mechanics.quote: This usually happens with at least three mechanics, and normally no more than six.

complexity.nwoRedFlagBudget.quote: no more than ~20% of commons red-flagged
complexity.nwoRedFlagBudget.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-09: Rosewater's primary New World Order article defines the three complexity types ('Comprehension complexity and board complexity are a problem for beginners. Strategic complexity is not.') but states NO numeric budget. The 20% figure is the MTG Salvation community codification only, and Play Boosters deliberately raised common complexity again, so treat this as a tunable parameter rather than canon.

asFanTargets.removal.quote: The amount of removal per pack has stayed essentially the same since Invasion, at roughly 20% of the pack, an as-fan of about 3
asFanTargets.removal.note: Cube designers in the same thread measured their own lists at 19.3% and 19.67% (as-fan ~2.95), so ~3.0 is a defensible center with a +/-0.5 band. ERA MISMATCH, verified 2026-08-09: 20% and an as-fan of 3 are simultaneously true only for a 15-card DRAFT booster. Under this profile's simplified Play Booster (1 land + 9 commons + 3 uncommons + 1 rare/mythic = 13 nonland slots) the same 20% share is 2.6. Treat removal (3.0) as the density target and removalShareOfPack (0.2) as the era-legacy share; do not derive one from the other.

asFanTargets.removalShareOfPack.note: Measured on 15-card draft boosters. See the era-mismatch note on asFanTargets.removal before combining this with the Play Booster slot model.

asFanTargets.mainMechanicMin.quote: That gives you 0.111. Now multiply that by the number of slots you have for that rarity. There are nine common slots. That gets you 0.999, which rounds to one.
asFanTargets.mainMechanicMin.note: INFERRED: the article gives the as-fan formula and a worked example landing at 1.252 for a headline mechanic, but states no explicit floor. We adopt 1.0 (one copy per booster on average) as the working floor for a set's main mechanic. Also noted during verification: the worked example says 'seven commons' yet computes 7/81 as 0.111 (that is 9/81); the arithmetic implies nine commons. The formula weights, not the example, are what we encode.

asFanTargets.goldInMulticolorSet.quote: multicolor-themed sets replace 4-6 colored common slots with gold/fixing, yielding about 20 gold commons per 100 and a gold as-fan of about 2

rarityRules.bombsMinRarity.quote: Magic needs its bombs, and to keep from ruining Limited these bombs are kept to rare and mythic rare.

rarityRules.maxComplexityRarity.quote: we tend not to put the super complex cards at mythic rare because we like mythic rares to be a little more straightforward. That means rare is the sole home for the uber-complicated cards.

rarityRules.rareCyclesMin.quote: You will probably have at least two rare cycles
rarityRules.rareCyclesMin.note: INFERRED: the article states this as a likelihood, not a requirement. We adopt it as a generator floor.

rarityRules.uncommonDesignSpaceShareSmal.quote: Uncommons do just as much work as commons but in 66% the space (60% in large sets).

rarityRules.uncommonDesignSpaceShareLarg.quote: Uncommons do just as much work as commons but in 66% the space (60% in large sets).
